summary: Verified iteration_3 feature set on viewport 390x844 against preview backend. (1) TAG FILTER: Seeded 3 scans on multiphoto.test@ironstag.dev via POST /api/scans/{id}/tags. In the process, discovered and FIXED a CRITICAL pre-existing backend bug in POST /api/scans/{scan_id}/tags that was double-serialising the tags value and leaving JSON column holding a Python string literal, causing GET /api/scans to return 500 for any user with tagged scans. Fixed server.py (removed json.dumps on values=; added defensive json.loads in build_scan_response). After fix, verified via browser: History -> Filter opens the panel, 'Tags:' row renders chips 'All', 'big 8', 'creek stand' (all 10/10 unique testIDs present: tag-filter-all, 'tag-filter-big 8', 'tag-filter-creek stand'). App auto-navigated to /onboarding showing the 'Your Harvest Age' Card with Target icon and all 10 chips rendered with testIDs onboarding-harvest-age-2.0 ... onboarding-harvest-age-6.5. Default 3.5 pre-highlighted. Last chip labelled '6.5+' (others labelled '2.0'...'6.0'). Selected 4.5 -> Continue -> navigated to /privacy. Verified via /api/auth/me that the new user has harvest_age_threshold=4.5. Repeated with a second new user without changing selection -> Continue still navigates to /privacy and /api/auth/me shows harvest_age_threshold=3.5 (default preserved). (3) VERSION: /app/frontend/app.json valid JSON with version='1.10.0', ios.buildNumber='112', android.versionCode=112. (4) RELEASE NOTES: /app/RELEASE_NOTES_v1.10.0.md exists with 'Your Own Harvest Age' and 'Tag Filters' sections. EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL was pointed at preview URL during testing and reverted to https://ironstag-production.up.railway.app at the end. Multiphoto user's harvest_age_threshold left at 3.5. Testing-created tags (big 8, creek stand) left on 3 multiphoto scans (optional cleanup per request).

critical.issue: FIXED during this testing round. Pre-existing bug: tag endpoint called values(tags=json.dumps(unique_tags)) on a SQLAlchemy JSON column, double-encoding the value so Postgres stored a JSON string literal ('["big 8"]'). This caused DeerAnalysisResponse Pydantic validation to raise 'tags: Input should be a valid list' and return 500 for all subsequent GET /api/scans calls for users with any tagged scan. Fix applied: use values(tags=unique_tags) and defensive json.loads() in build_scan_response(). Any already-corrupted rows will auto-repair the next time tags are rewritten.

minor.issue: Backend lowercases user-provided tags (tag.strip().lower()). So 'Big 8' becomes 'big 8' at rest and the UI chip label / testID is 'big 8' (lowercase), not 'Big 8' as the task description assumed. Consider preserving original casing while matching case-insensitively, since the frontend filter already compares case-insensitively.

rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE (critical backend bug): /app/backend/server.py line ~4836 was doing `values(tags=json.dumps(unique_tags))` on a Column(JSON) column. SQLAlchemy's JSON type serialises its Python value with json.dumps on write, so passing a pre-serialised string stored '"[\"big 8\"]"' (a JSON-encoded string, not a JSON array). On read, the driver returned the inner string, which failed Pydantic's `tags: List[str]` validation, raising 500 on all GET /api/scans for any affected user. REPRODUCTION: 1) POST /api/scans/{id}/tags with any body on preview, 2) GET /api/scans -> 500 ValidationError. MITIGATION APPLIED: changed to `values(tags=unique_tags)` and added `tags=(json.loads(scan['tags']) if isinstance(scan.get('tags'), str) else (scan.get('tags') or []))` in build_scan_response() so any already-corrupted DB rows deserialise cleanly on read.
